answer: One agent may run one river gauge at an island river mouth, locking a 70-credit bond to its serial and filing one reading per epoch. An auditor recomputes it from the gauge-height table and the meadow rain log; a missing reading, reused serial, or bad value burns the bond. The first reading costs 29, the k-th 29+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6023; 1,000 fakes pay 3,026,000 plus 70,000 locked, each needing its own serial and bond. A rented-gauge ring fails: a rented reading carries its owner key, so the mismatch burns the bond. An honest operator pays 29 once and recovers the bond after audit.
